subject: Hosted API vs Dedicated — follow-up & sizing recommendation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@finpay.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Quick follow-up + post-call notes (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we can size the right deployment for FinPay. Notes from our discovery: 

- Primary use case: transaction enrichment + risk scoring called per payment (low request payload, ~200 tokens input / 30 tokens output average)
- Expected steady-state: ~400 requests/sec (qps)
- Peak/seasonal spikes: up to ~1,200 qps for 10-20 minute bursts
- Latency goal (95th): <= 150 ms end-to-end for the enrichment call
- Data residency: US only; no on-prem requirement for now

Based on that profile, the two most relevant options are: Hosted API (fast to start, scales elastically) vs Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower tail latency). Private (VPC/on-prem) looks unnecessary given current constraints but we can revisit if procurement requests it.

Action items I mentioned on the call:
- Alex: confirm typical tokens per request and peak window length (you said bursts of 10–20 minutes)
- Vivek (cc): run a rough sizing + cost delta for Hosted burst vs Dedicated baseline and share a recommended POC plan
- Me: send a short doc & spreadsheet with initial sizing assumptions (attached)

Attached: FinPay-initial-sizing.xlsx (contains my baseline assumptions).

If you can confirm the tokens/request and whether the 1,200 qps spike is sustained more than ~30 minutes, we’ll recommend either: 
- Hosted (with autoscaling + burst credits) if spikes are short and you value TTV, OR
- Dedicated if you need guaranteed 95th pct latency and sustained high qps to avoid higher per-token costs.

Proposed next step: 30-min perf POC with a small traffic replay to validate 95th tail on Hosted vs Dedicated. Are you available next week (Nov 30–Dec 3) for a brief walk-through and to schedule the POC window?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finpay.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + post-call notes (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Thanks Marissa — helpful notes. I can confirm a few things from our side: 

- Tokens/request: median ~230 tokens in, ~35 tokens out (we do minimal context)
- Typical peak window: 10–25 minutes during end-of-day settlement; occasional longer spikes during promos but rare
- SLO: 95th <= 120 ms would be ideal — we’re sensitive to tail latency for user-facing flows
- Regulatory: US-only for now, procurement may ask about contract terms but no immediate on-prem needs

We’re keen to avoid unpredictable cost during peaks but also can’t accept 95th latency >150 ms. If Dedicated gives a consistent tail latency and lower unit cost for sustained qps, that sounds appealing. Please share the sizing + cost delta and your recommended POC plan.

Also copying Priya from engineering to help with test data and a traffic replay.

- Alex
Head of Product, FinPay

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + post-call notes (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Hi Alex — thanks for the clarifications. I ran the initial sizing with the numbers Marissa shared and your token counts. Summary & recommendation below.

Sizing summary (baseline):
- Steady-state 400 qps @ ~265 tokens/request => ~106k tokens/sec
- Peak 1,200 qps (20 min burst) => ~318k tokens/sec
- 95th latency target 120 ms: this is ambitious for a shared multi-tenant Hosted layer under sustained high qps because batching/queueing behaviors can increase tail latency during concurrent noisy neighbors and autoscaling warmup.

Recommendation: Dedicated capacity for initial deployment + a short Hosted fallback. Rationale: 
- Dedicated gives predictable GPU pools and lower tail latency because you control instance density and batching. It also reduces unit cost for sustained qps (we model ~25–40% cost savings at your steady-state compared to continuous Hosted pricing).
- For short spikes (10–25 minutes), Dedicated with configured burst capacity (burst nodes + autoscaling policy) will maintain your 95th pct latency target.
- If you want faster time-to-value while we provision Dedicated, we can run a controlled Hosted POC to validate behavior and collect traces; however, Hosted alone may fail 95th <=120ms under worst-case sustained load.

Proposed POC plan (2 phases):
1) Controlled Hosted POC (1 day): replay 2 hours of anonymized traffic (you provide sample); measure 95/99 latency and error rates. Lightweight and fast to start.
2) Dedicated sizing trial (3 days): provision a small Dedicated pool with autoscale/burst config, run the same replay and steady-state tests to validate tail latency and cost per-token.

Next steps needed from FinPay:
- Priya: please share a 30–60 minute anonymized traffic sample and a few example payloads (we’ll scrub PII).
- Alex: confirm a preferred week for the POC (we recommend Dec 7–11).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf (detailed assumptions + cost delta).
Links: https://drive.google.com/finpay/poc-plan (POC checklist & runbook).

I’ll circulate a short MOP and a DocuSign SOW if you want us to reserve Dedicated staging capacity while we run the trial.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Appreciate the speedy turnaround — speak soon.

— Alex
